narrative_purpose: Kills the intuition that a bigger breath makes a better diver: a human keeps a quarter of its oxygen as lung air, a seal almost none, loading it into blood and muscle instead.
subject: Two swimming bodies shown side by side in cutaway against the same dark water, both semi-transparent so their interiors read. On the left, a slender human-proportioned swimmer whose chest cavity glows brightly with a large pale luminous air space, while the vessels through the torso glow moderately and the limb muscles are only faintly lit. On the right, a thickset barrel-bodied seal-like marine animal whose chest cavity is small and nearly dark, while a dense network of vessels through its body glows intensely and its thick swimming muscles along the back and tail glow a deep saturated colour throughout.
scene: One continuous stretch of open blue-black water, both animals at the same depth and scaled so their bodies occupy similar frame height.
camera: Straight-on side view of both cutaways at equal visual weight.
light: Internal glow is the only strong light source in each body — pale luminous air in the left chest, deep crimson and cyan through the right animal's vessels and muscle; cool ambient blue-green from above.
palette: Void indigo water, pale mist for lung air, crimson and magenta for blood-rich tissue, cyan accents, deep teal shadow.
style: Painterly naturalist cutaway plate, glowing from within, hand-painted texture.
detail_level: Crisp on the size difference between the two chest cavities and on the density of glow in the right animal's swimming muscle; outer body contours softened.
composition: Left animal in the left half, right animal in the right half, open low-detail dark water in a band across the top of each for overlay labels.
consistency_notes: The left chest cavity must be visibly large and bright, the right visibly small and dim — that inversion is the entire point. The right animal is a generic thickset marine diver, not a recognisable Earth species portrait.
negative_prompt: no text, no labels, no numbers, no bar charts or percentages, no arrows, no panel borders, no photographic or 3D-render look, no cartoon style
